html:
The Guna, who call themselves Gunadule, are an Indigenous people of eastern Panama and northwestern Colombia. This map territory covers their land around the Gulf of Urabá and the Darién forest; most Guna today live on the San Blas islands of Guna Yala.

They speak a Chibchan language. In the 1500s they lived inland in the Darién and moved toward the Caribbean coast and islands over the following centuries. They fished, farmed and traded coconuts, and are known for the mola, a cloth panel of layered, cut and sewn fabric worn by women.

In 1925, when Panama tried to suppress their customs, the Guna rose in the Guna Revolution and won autonomy. Guna Yala became a self governing territory in 1938. Other Guna lands include Madungandí; the Emberá and Wounaan are their neighbours in the Darién.
